title: 2004 AMC 8 Problem 17
statement: Three friends have a total of \(6\) identical pencils, and each one has at least one pencil. In how many ways can this happen?

solutions.text:
First give each friend one pencil. Then \(3\) pencils remain to distribute among the \(3\) friends.

If one friend gets all \(3\) remaining pencils, there are \(3\) ways. If the remaining pencils split as \(2\) and \(1,\) there are \(3\cdot2=6\) ways. If each friend gets one more, there is \(1\) way.

The total number of ways is \(3+6+1=10.\)

Thus, D is the correct answer.
hints: Give each friend one pencil first.
Count the ways to distribute the remaining \(3\) pencils among the \(3\) friends.
